items.difficultyReason: On supplied axes the student transfers centre-frequency pairs into touching histogram bars, joins their top midpoints to make a polygon, and interprets a grouped frequency as a class count rather than an exact value. These are linked familiar procedures and an interpretation, with the table and scales provided.
items.independentDerivation: The five frequencies sum to 12 months. With the taught equal-width, touching-bar convention, the centres 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 are 10 apart, giving bars over 5–15, 15–25, 25–35, 35–45 and 45–55 at heights 2, 3, 1, 2 and 4. The polygon joins (10,2), (20,3), (30,1), (40,2), (50,4), with zero endpoints (0,0) and (60,0), matching the source solution. Three months lie in the class centred on 20; the data do not establish that exactly 20 cakes were sold in those months. The question table, axes, title, scales and both asks match the source; the unfilled answer bars retain the source geometry. Both answer editions use the supplied solution graph and the correct explanation.
items.classWidthInterpretation: The centres alone do not logically prove class boundaries for arbitrary grouped data. In this instructional context, however, p8 teaches touching equal-width bars centred on class centres, p9 applies this to histograms and polygons, and the regularly spaced centres and supplied source answer consistently indicate width 10. That ordinary convention is a sufficient interpretation for this task, without adding an explicit student given or claiming approval of one. The historical hold remains recorded and is not retroactively resolved.
